subject: Wavefront live-output stalls during burst — urgent SLA risk
messages:
From: Simon Lee <simon@wavefront.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@wavefront.ai>, support@wavefront.ai
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live stream hang during 10k concurrent requests — urgent

Marissa —

We're hitting sustained hangs on the live token stream when we push burst traffic (~10k concurrent sessions). Tokens stop arriving for 8–12s intermittently, then resume. This started after yesterday's load increase and we're seeing elevated 5xxs and websocket timeouts. Customer UX is failing; our product shows a progress spinner and then times out.

We've attached a small pcap excerpt and server-side logs. Key notes:
- Error spike aligns with 2028-05-21T22:03:xxZ
- Client reports WebSocket close code 1006 at the same time
- Throughput stays high, but chunk emission becomes irregular and then pauses

Can Redwood ops confirm whether this is throttling in the proxy layer or something in your runtime? We're on a dedicated cluster (region us-west-2). This is blocking our launch and we need a call.

--
Simon Lee
SRE, Wavefront Analytics

From: david_kim@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 15:52:00 -07:00

On Mon, May 21, 2028 at 03:35 PM, marissa_cole@redwood.com wrote:
> Simon — thanks for the signal and the logs. I'm pulling David and Grace onto this thread now.

Quick initial findings from the attached logs:
- Proxy (edge-gw-7) shows repeated HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer stalls where the upstream kept connection open but emitted zero bytes for 9–11s before a small chunk.
- No obvious CPU/GPU exhaustion on the model hosts during the window; memory and GPU utilization look steady.
- We see a surge in queued requests on the routing tier that correlates with increased per-connection latency and a spike in our internal circuit-breaker counter.

Hypothesis: a queuing/backpressure interaction between the routing tier and the proxy's chunk flush interval is amplifying jitter into observable token-free gaps in the socket stream. Possible contributing factors:
- proxy keepalive/flush timers not tuned for bursty multiplexed sessions
- routing tier batching causing request reordering and head-of-line stalls

I'll attach an extraction of the 22:03Z traces to the Drive link. Next steps:
- Grace to confirm whether KV cache thrash could increase completion variance.
- If confirmed, we should try a temporary proxy config tweak (reduce chunk flush window, increase concurrency) and validate in a canary.

-David
Principal Infra Engineer
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live stream hang during 10k concurrent requests — urgent

Folks —

I completed a quick runbook check and lightweight replay against a staging capture:
- KV cache hit-rate degraded from ~93% to ~54% during the burst window, likely due to some prompt variability that increases cache churn. That increases variance on model load from 20–40ms to bursts of 120–220ms when cache misses cascade.
- Model runtime threads were healthy; Gpu latency p99 moved from 45ms to 160ms for a subset of requests that missed cache.

Combining David's routing observations + cache thrash gives a plausible amplification path: increased model-service latency -> longer request handling -> routing backlog -> proxy chunk flush stalls -> client-visible token gaps.

Immediate mitigations proposed (canary first):
1) Shorten proxy chunk flush interval from 10s -> 2s for the Wavefront routing policy.
2) Increase routing-tier concurrency for this customer's ded. pool by 25%.
3) Enable conservative KV cache prefetch for the most common prompt templates (we have a quick toggle).

I can run 1+2 in a canary today; need ops approval for the canary window. I'll prepare the rollout playbook and attach MAP draft.

- Grace
Lead Backend Reliability Engineer
From: Simon Lee <simon@wavefront.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Nair <priya@wavefront.ai>, support@wavefront.ai
Date: Wed, 23 May 2028 19:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live stream hang during 10k concurrent requests — urgent

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the quick triage and the canary run earlier today. We validated the short proxy flush + routing concurrency tweak in a controlled window and saw the token gaps drop to background levels (p99 gap < 300ms). The customer is still sensitive: they reported two more small incidents during a large synthetic test yesterday, so they're asking for an executive-facing summary and a timeline to permanent fix.

Impact summary for execs:
- Business impact: Live transcription experience interrupted for ~15% of sessions during large bursts; potential SLA credit exposure.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): cache-thrash-amplified routing backlog + proxy chunk flush behavior under burst.
- Short-term mitigation: proxy flush reduction + routing concurrency increase (canary verified).
- Medium-term work: improve KV cache prefetching, make chunk flush adaptive, and add routing-tier backpressure controls.

Can we get a concise executive note (1 page) and a proposed delivery timeline (weeks) so I can escalate internally? Wavefront Legal and Procurement are requesting proposed SLA remediation steps and a signoff path.

--
Simon
SRE, Wavefront Analytics
